l: kings and people of the earth, Revelation, Chapter 13
s: The earth's inhabitants marvel at the first beast after its wound is healed and worship the dragon and the beast, asking who is like the beast and who can make war with it. All who dwell on the earth will worship the beast except those whose names are written in the book of life of the Lamb. They are deceived by the second beast's signs, urged to make an image, and made to bear the mark.

God is the target of the first beast's blasphemy, which is directed against his name, his dwelling, and those who dwell in heaven. The beast's authority and its forty-two months of war are described as given to it. The book of life belongs to the Lamb who has been killed, and its names were written from the foundation of the world.

In Chapter 14 the narrator sees the Lamb standing on Mount Zion with the 144,000, who bear the names of the Lamb and his Father on their foreheads and alone can learn a new song sung before the throne. Three angels then fly or follow with proclamations: the first announces an eternal Good News and the hour of God's judgment, the second announces the fall of Babylon the great, and the third warns that worshippers of the beast and his image, and those who receive his mark, will drink the wine of God's wrath and be tormented forever. A voice from heaven declares blessed the dead who die in the Lord. The chapter closes with a harvest scene in which one like a son of man on a white cloud reaps the earth with a sickle, and another angel gathers the earth's grape clusters and throws them into the great wine press of the wrath of God, from which blood flows up to the horses' bridles for 1,600 stadia.

The Lamb is seen standing on Mount Zion with the 144,000, who have his name and his Father's name on their foreheads. The 144,000 follow him wherever he goes, and those who worship the beast are tormented in his presence and that of the holy angels.

l: one hundred forty-four thousand, Revelation, Chapter 14
s: The 144,000 stand with the Lamb on Mount Zion, bearing his name and his Father's name on their foreheads. They alone can learn the new song sung before the throne, and they are described as redeemed from the earth, virgins not defiled with women, followers of the Lamb, first fruits to God and the Lamb, with no lie in their mouth and blameless.

God is the Father whose name is written on the foreheads of the 144,000, and he is to be feared, glorified and worshipped as maker of heaven, earth, sea and springs of water. His wrath is prepared as unmixed wine in the cup of his anger, and the great wine press of his wrath is trodden outside the city.

The first angel flies in mid heaven with an eternal Good News for every nation, tribe, language and people. He cries with a loud voice to fear and glorify God and worship the Creator, because the hour of his judgment has come.
A second angel declares that Babylon the great has fallen. She is said to have made all the nations drink the wine of the wrath of her sexual immorality.
The beast and his image are worshipped by those who receive his mark on forehead or hand. Those who worship him are warned by the third angel of torment and God's wrath.

l: people with the mark of the beast, Revelation, Chapter 14
s: Those who worship the beast and his image and receive his mark will drink the wine of God's wrath, unmixed in the cup of his anger. They will be tormented with fire and sulfur before the holy angels and the Lamb, the smoke of their torment rising forever, with no rest day or night.

One like a son of man is seen sitting on a white cloud, with a golden crown on his head and a sharp sickle in his hand. When an angel from the temple tells him the harvest is ripe, he thrusts his sickle on the earth and the earth is reaped.

l: great wine press of the wrath of God, Revelation, Chapter 14
s: An angel gathers the vintage of the earth and throws it into the great wine press of the wrath of God. The press is trodden outside the city, and blood comes out of it up to the horses' bridles for 1,600 stadia.

l: harvest of the earth, Revelation, Chapter 14
s: An angel from the temple announces that the hour to reap has come and the harvest of the earth is ripe. The earth is reaped by the one on the cloud, and then the earth's grape clusters, fully ripe, are gathered by another angel with a sharp sickle and thrown into the wine press.

The first angel proclaims that the hour of God's judgment has come. It is shown in Babylon's fall, in the torment of the beast's worshippers, and in the reaping of the earth and the treading of the wine press of God's wrath.

The narrator sees a great and marvelous sign in heaven: seven angels holding the seven last plagues, which complete God's wrath. He also sees those who overcame the beast, his image, and the number of his name standing on a sea of glass mixed with fire, holding harps of God. They sing the song of Moses and the Lamb, praising God's works and ways and declaring that all nations will come and worship him. The heavenly temple is then opened, and the seven angels come out in pure bright linen with golden sashes. One of the four living creatures gives them seven golden bowls full of God's wrath, and the temple fills with smoke from God's glory and power so that no one can enter until the seven plagues are finished.

The seven angels are seen in the sky as a great and marvelous sign, holding the seven last plagues. They come out of the opened heavenly temple clothed in pure, bright linen with golden sashes around their chests, and one of the four living creatures gives them seven golden bowls full of God's wrath.
The seven last plagues are held by the seven angels, and in them God's wrath is finished. No one can enter the temple until these plagues are completed.

God is praised as Lord God, the Almighty, King of the nations, whose works are great and marvelous and whose ways are righteous and true. He is declared the only holy one, whose righteous acts have been revealed and before whom all nations will come to worship. He lives forever and ever, and his glory and power fill the temple with smoke.
God's wrath is said to be finished in the seven last plagues. It is contained in seven golden bowls given to the seven angels.

l: overcomers (those who overcame the beast), Revelation, Chapter 15
s: Those who overcame the beast, his image, and the number of his name are seen standing on a sea of glass mixed with fire. They hold harps of God and sing the song of Moses and the Lamb.

l: song of Moses and the Lamb, Revelation, Chapter 15
s: The overcomers sing this song, which declares God's works great and marvelous and his ways righteous and true. It asks who would not fear and glorify him, proclaims him alone holy, and says all nations will come and worship because his righteous acts have been revealed.

l: temple of the tabernacle of the testimony, Revelation, Chapter 15
s: The temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven is opened, and the seven angels come out of it. It is then filled with smoke from God's glory and power, and no one can enter until the seven plagues are finished.
Seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God are given to the seven angels by one of the four living creatures.

A loud voice from the temple commands the seven angels to pour out the seven bowls of God's wrath on the earth. The first four bowls bring sores on those with the mark of the beast, blood in the sea, blood in the rivers and springs, and scorching heat from the sun, while the angel of the waters and the altar affirm God's judgments as righteous. The fifth bowl darkens the beast's throne and kingdom, and the sixth dries up the Euphrates so the kings from the sunrise can come, as three unclean spirits from the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet gather the kings to the place called Harmagedon. The seventh bowl is poured into the air, a voice declares "It is done!", and a great earthquake splits the great city, topples the cities of the nations, and removes islands and mountains. Babylon the great is remembered by God, and huge hailstones fall on people, who still blaspheme God.

The seven angels are commanded by a loud voice from the temple to pour out the seven bowls of God's wrath on the earth. Each in turn pours out his bowl, on the earth, sea, rivers and springs, sun, the beast's throne, the Euphrates, and the air.

l: seven bowls of the wrath of God, Revelation, Chapter 16
s: The bowls are poured out one after another, bringing sores, blood in the sea and waters, scorching heat, darkness on the beast's kingdom, the drying of the Euphrates, and finally a great earthquake and hail. They are the means of God's judgment on the earth.

God is praised as righteous and true in his judgments by the angel of the waters and by the altar, because those who shed the blood of saints and prophets are given blood to drink. He is described as having power over the plagues, yet people blaspheme him and do not repent or give him glory. He remembers Babylon the great to give her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath.

l: people with the mark of the beast, Revelation, Chapter 16
s: Those who had the mark of the beast and worshiped his image are afflicted with harmful and painful sores from the first bowl. Along with others, they are scorched, blaspheme God for their pains and sores, and refuse to repent of their works.

The beast's throne is struck by the fifth bowl, and his kingdom is darkened. A spirit-like frog comes out of his mouth, along with those from the dragon and the false prophet, to gather the kings for war.
Harmagedon is the place, called so in Hebrew, where the kings of the whole inhabited earth are gathered together. They are gathered for the war of the great day of God the Almighty.
When the seventh bowl is poured out, Babylon the great is remembered in the sight of God. She is to be given the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath.

The great earthquake follows the seventh bowl, with lightnings, sounds, and thunders. It is described as greater than any since men have been on the earth, dividing the great city into three parts, felling the cities of the nations, and causing every island to flee and the mountains to vanish.
